title: Spectrum of statin hepatotoxicity: experience of the drug-induced liver injury network
authors: Russo MW, Hoofnagle JH, Gu J, Fontana RJ, Barnhart H, Kleiner DE, et al.
population: Cases of drug-induced liver injury attributed to a statin among 1188 cases enrolled 2004 to 2012 in the prospective US Drug Induced Liver Injury Network registry
funder: DILIN is supported by the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases under cooperative agreements 1UO1DK065201, 1UO1DK065193, 1UO1DKO65184, 1UO1DK065211, 1UO1DK065238 and 1UO1DK06F5176; supported in part by the Intramural Research Program of the NIH, National Cancer Institute.
authorConflicts: Two NIDDK employees took part in design, analysis and editing; several investigators reported speaking, consultancy or research support from pharmaceutical companies, including Merck.
result: 22 of 1188 drug-induced liver injury cases were attributed to a statin; all commonly used statins were implicated. Median age 60 (41 to 80), 68% female; latency 34 days to 10 years (median 155 days); median peak ALT 892 U/L and bilirubin 6.1 mg/dL. Nine had cholestatic hepatitis and 12 hepatocellular injury, 6 of these with an autoimmune phenotype. Nine were hospitalised, 4 developed hepatic failure and 1 died; 4 (18%) developed chronic liver injury, 3 of them with an autoimmune phenotype. Mild aminotransferase rises occur in up to 3% of treated patients.
